notes: Read all targets and full context. Resolve constitutional and fiscal jurisdiction to the U.S. federal government, and anchor current finances and the unnamed opposing party to the 2008 source. Preserve the unnamed opponent as a contextualized role rather than inventing a proper name. Separate commitments, allegations about opponents, spending figures and causal characterizations. Omit the heading.

claims.claim_text: Support for restricting the U.S. federal government to its legitimate constitutional functions.
Support for a U.S. federal government that empowers people while limiting intrusion into their lives.
Support for federal spending only as necessary and taxation only to fund essential government functions.
Support for enabling enterprise, innovation and civic initiative.
Opposition to treating government as a substitute for family or community.
The opposing U.S. party in the 2008 Republican platform is portrayed as favoring greater government control over people's lives and earnings.
The opposing U.S. party in the 2008 Republican platform is portrayed as supporting continued politically targeted spending.
Opposition to politically targeted government spending regardless of which party practices it.
The opposing U.S. party in the 2008 Republican platform is portrayed as ignoring fiscal problems while wasting billions on ineffective programs.
Commitment to end wasteful U.S. spending on ineffective programs.
The federal political establishment in 2008 is characterized by entrenched, intrusive tax-and-spend liberalism.
Commitment to challenge and defeat entrenched, intrusive federal tax-and-spend liberalism.
At the time of the 2008 platform, the U.S. federal government collects $2.7 trillion annually from families and businesses, equivalent to $7.4 billion daily.
At the time of the 2008 platform, the U.S. federal government spends over $3 trillion annually, equivalent to $8.2 billion daily.

Refusal by the architects of federal government expansion to acknowledge mistakes or abolish programs is characterized as a major reason for U.S. federal spending above $3 trillion annually at the time of the 2008 platform.
